old: A 1918 20 Pfennig from Germany. Large 20 in oak wreath, date 1918 (eagle or obverse mint letter often on the other side). Struck in iron (WWI-era emergency Notgeld family).
new: A 1918 20 Heller from the Austrian Empire (previously cataloged as a German 20 Pfennig). Large 20 in oak wreath with date 1918 below on the reverse, crowned double-headed Austrian eagle on the obverse (Stefan Schwartz). Struck in iron during WWI.
source: checked against https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces6133.html (Numista N#6133, KM# 2826) and photo C023_rev.webp (C023_Germany_1918_20Pfennig_rev.jpeg): the coin shown in C023_rev.webp is an exact match for the 1918 Austrian Empire 20 Heller in iron (Emperor Charles I, engraver Stefan Schwartz: large 20 inside oak wreath with 1918 below on reverse, crowned double-headed Austrian eagle on obverse, no country or currency legend), not a German Empire 20 Pfennig Notgeld

old: A ca. 1970s miniature “penny” in printed cardboard flap novelty slug token from USA. Card NEW NIXON PENNY, AND GETTING SMALLER, miniature cent in window. Struck in tiny copper-tone slug (~¼¢ size).
new: A ca. 1970s miniature “penny” in printed cardboard flap novelty slug token from USA. Card NEW NIXON PENNY, AND GETTING SMALLER, miniature cent in window. Struck in tiny copper-tone slug (~¼¢ size).
source: checked against https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces326399.html (Numista N#326399, 1974 7.5 mm miniature Lincoln cent 'Nixon Penny'; see also https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces109637.html N#109637) and photo T004_USA_ND_Nixon-Penny.jpeg: all claims hold (printed cardboard holder reading NEW NIXON PENNY and AND GETTING SMALLER with tiny ~1/4-cent copper-tone miniature Lincoln cent in the window)
